anomalies.observed: The anode of LED D1 (pin 2) is connected to net /Microcontroller/NET0014, which also contains U5.13 (ESP32 GPIO1), U11.1 (TPS1H200 IN), and U11.2 (TPS1H200 DIAG_EN). The heater output net Net-(J9-Pin_2) contains only U11.7 (TPS1H200 OUT) and J9.2 (heater connector).
anomalies.expected: Per the specification, the heater status LED and its series resistor should be on the HEATER net, which is the output net connected to U11.7 and J9.2. The LED should therefore be connected to Net-(J9-Pin_2), not to the GPIO1 control net.

evidence.quote: A status LED (D2) and series resistor (R3) are also on the `HEATER` net, so the heater output doubles as a visual "heater on" indicator at the board level

anomalies.impact: The LED will indicate the state of the control signal (GPIO1) rather than the actual heater output. If the TPS1H200 smart switch faults and turns off the heater while GPIO1 remains high, the LED will still be lit, falsely indicating that the heater is on. This defeats the intended visual heater-on indication.

parsed.summary: The design files contain an anomaly: the heater status LED D1 is connected to the GPIO1 control net instead of the heater output net, so it indicates the control signal rather than the actual heater state.
